topic.title: Writing a Simple Program
topic.description: Creating basic Java programs step by step

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s build your first Java program together! You’ll learn how to turn a simple idea into working code.

• How to structure a basic Java program
• How to store and use data with variables
• How to make your program interactive

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Writing a Simple Program works:

steps.title: Declare Variables
steps.description: First, we create containers (variables) to store our data. Like labeling jars for flour and sugar.
steps.code:
double radius; // Jar for radius
double area;   // Jar for area

steps.title: Assign Values
steps.description: Now we put something in our jars. Here we’re using a fixed radius of 20.
steps.code: radius = 20; // Put 20 in the radius jar

steps.title: Calculate & Display
steps.description: We mix our ingredients (calculate area) and show the result. Like baking and serving the cake!
steps.code:
area = radius * radius * 3.14159;
System.out.println("Area is " + area);

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Every Java program needs a `main` method - it’s the starting point
✓ Variables are like labeled jars that store data

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Start with a simple outline before coding
Use descriptive variable names (like `radius` instead of `r`)
Add comments to explain your code
donts: Don’t forget semicolons at the end of statements
Don’t use spaces in variable names (use `camelCase` instead)
Don’t skip testing your program with different inputs
sections.protip: Always compile and run your program after each small change - it’s easier to find mistakes!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Writing a Simple Program used in real apps?

examples.how: Calculate interest rates using similar formulas
Convert steps to calories burned using basic math
Convert temperatures between Celsius and Fahrenheit

problem.description: Write a program that calculates the area of a rectangle. Ask the user for length and width, then display the area.
hints: Declare variables for length and width
Use input.nextDouble() to get user input
problem.explanation: We first get the length and width from the user, then multiply them to get the area. The Scanner class helps us read user input.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Java programs start with a class and main method
📌 Variables store data like containers store ingredients
📌 Always test your program with different inputs
📌 You’re ready to make interactive programs next!
